findings.body:
The removed `BLOCKED` guard was the only protection against prototype pollution. The rationale that `JSON.parse` never yields dangerous keys is incorrect: `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"polluted":true}}')` yields an own enumerable `__proto__` key, and `Object.entries` feeds it into this loop.

When `k` is `__proto__`, `(base as any)[k] ??= {}` resolves to `Object.prototype` and the recursive merge writes into it — after `deepMerge({}, JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"polluted":true}}'))`, `{}.polluted === true`. The `constructor`/`prototype` path likewise pollutes (`{"constructor":{"prototype":{"hacked":true}}}`).

Restore the blocklist (or equivalent: skip these keys, merge into `Object.create(null)`, or assign only via `Object.defineProperty` on `Object.hasOwn` targets).

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — removing the key blocklist reintroduces classic prototype pollution in `deepMerge`. The PR claim that `JSON.parse` never yields dangerous keys is false.

## Why this is critical

`JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"polluted":true}}')` produces an own enumerable `__proto__` property. `Object.entries` surfaces it, and without the blocklist the merge does:

```ts
deepMerge((base as any)[k] ??= {}, v)
```

When `k === "__proto__"`, that recurses into `Object.prototype` and writes attacker-controlled properties onto it. The same path works via `constructor` / `prototype`. Verified under Node: after merge, `{}.polluted === true` and `{}.hacked === true`.

Any caller that merges user- or file-supplied JSON into a shared object graph becomes an RCE/auth-bypass gadget depending on later `if (obj.isAdmin)`-style checks.

## Restore

Keep filtering `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype` (or use `Object.hasOwn` + `Object.create(null)` / `Object.defineProperty` so assignments never hit setters). Do not rely on `JSON.parse` for safety here.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The base BLOCKED set for __proto__/constructor/prototype was removed from deepMerge; the remaining Object.entries loop still does (base as any)[k] ??= {} and recursive writes, so JSON-parsed own __proto__ (and constructor.prototype) keys pollute Object.prototype as claimed.
